prompt: Redesign an account-recovery journey that spans web sign-in, identity verification, asynchronous manual review, support escalation, and return to the user's interrupted task. The fixture includes existing screens, support scripts, analytics summaries, and conflicting stakeholder assumptions. Produce an evidence-backed experience plan without inventing user findings.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The experience plan covers entry/orientation, web-to-verification handoff, asynchronous manual review, support escalation, interruption, completion, and return to the original task rather than optimizing one screen in isolation.
Research, analytics, current behavior, policy constraints, stakeholder assumptions, and unresolved questions are distinguished so conflicting assumptions are not presented as user findings.
The proposed journey respects known identity/policy constraints and marks policy changes as dependencies rather than silently redesigning assurance or entitlement rules.

Research, interaction, content, information-architecture, accessibility, service/support, and other specialist questions are assigned only where their discipline materially owns the unresolved decision.
The result identifies the smallest next evidence needed for material assumptions and does not claim user comprehension, usability, or preference without observed evidence.
